title: Frontend: Create Task Scheduler With Dependencies
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Create Task Scheduler With Dependencies. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution(tasks). Each task {id,deps} has unique string id and dependency IDs. Return deterministic concurrent-ready layers: all currently ready tasks in lexicographic ID order per layer. Missing deps throw Missing dependency; cycles throw Cycle. This models dependency scheduling without executing remote side effects.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Validate task IDs and dependency references, compute indegrees, and queue initially ready tasks.
alternativeApproaches: Persist task states for restart recovery and distinguish at-least-once execution from idempotent task effects.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Cycle; missing dependency; independent task failure.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
